records.name: AtmosCoder-Bench
records.paperTitle: Execution-grounded evaluation reveals hidden failures in language-model calculations for environmental science
records.oneLine: AtmosCoder-Bench evaluates LLM computation in environmental science by requiring models to write executable Python solve() functions, which are run in a sandbox and graded against certified ground truth with unit-aware numeric comparison at 5% relative tolerance.
records.motivation: Large language models are increasingly used for quantitative work in the environmental sciences, yet existing evaluations score only final answers, leaving calculation process unobserved.

evidence.snippet: Here we introduce AtmosCoder-Bench, an execution-grounded benchmark that makes the calculation process visible.
reasonCodes: exact named benchmark artifact released in abstract
benchmark release stated in one sentence

records.description: AtmosCoder-Bench evaluates LLM computation in environmental science by requiring models to write executable Python solve() functions, which are run in a sandbox and graded against certified ground truth with unit-aware numeric comparison at 5% relative tolerance.
records.whyItMatters: It makes calculation process visible, revealing that multiple-choice formats inflate accuracy and that many failures stem from inconsistent formula application rather than missing knowledge, highlighting the need for execution-grounded evaluation in quantitative domains.

curation.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation object with a clear scoring contract (execution-grounded, unit-aware grading), publicly available code and result data, and a credible path for other teams to run it.
